issue: Deterministic keyboard W/S alternating reversal; reported slow U-turn and leftward drift

visual_evidence.version_caveat: Reference title is v1.0.3; recovered assets are v1.0.2. No exact version delta is established.

sequence.observed: Movement tutorial overlay in the dungeon. Text says the virtual stick can move the character around; a separate instruction describes touch controls. The gameplay view includes the player and virtual stick.
sequence.evidence_type: direct video frames sampled at 1-second intervals; the tutorial demonstrates general movement, not a keyboard reversal

sequence.observed: Gameplay HUD and virtual stick remain visible with the player on the stone walkway near the equipment tutorial sequence. The sampled frames do not expose input history or a clear alternating 180-degree reversal; no W/S-specific turn rate or lateral drift can be measured.
sequence.evidence_type: direct video frames sampled at 2 frames/second; no matched reversal inferred

visual_evidence.inference: The reference establishes camera-relative virtual-stick movement as the mobile interaction. It does not establish whether alternating W/S keyboard intent should be smoothed or whether the observed PC left arc is a defect.

logic_evidence.input: port/windows-foundation/features/platform_input/semantic_input.cpp:107-114 maps W minus S to move2D.y and normalizes only diagonals above unit length. Default PC policy runs while moving unless the configured run key is held. This is an intentional PC input adaptation; it is not original mobile dispatch.
logic_evidence.caller_order: port/windows-foundation/main.cpp around the gameplay input block first calls ActorMovement::steer_source_intent with the active camera basis, selects the resulting source locomotion alias, then CombatSession::update advances retained source animation. The retained frame callback delivers authored root motion through MotionHandler before main's source late-rotation step. The next frame's root displacement therefore uses the facing produced by the previous late rotation.
source: GameObject::UpdatePath at 0x3940c0 reads the same heading state; recovered handoff port/windows-foundation/reports/original-actor-heading-live.json records the call to ValidateDirection at 0x525d60 followed by SetHeadingDirection at 0x393be8 even when the validation result is diagnostic.

Move focus supplies flags 0x23c1 and movement type 0 in port/windows-foundation/original_actor_motion_flags.cpp. The source movement-policy handoff records bit7 as UpdatePath and bit0 as visual-position displacement.

Character::UpdateRotation at 0x393710 uses resolved property47 and source flag0x20; ordinary rotation is modifier*4pi radians/second. Exact antipodal headings retain the strict source wrap branches in port/level-world/actor_rotation.cpp.

RootSceneNode displacement at 0x35cf48 rotates local root displacement by the current visual facing. Existing port/windows-foundation/tests/source_reversal_probe.cpp and reports/source-reversal-diagnosis.json reproduce repeated world-left root arcs for alternating source headings without changing runtime code.
logic_evidence.current_runtime: main.cpp uses the same actor motor and CombatSession: input intent is steered before the retained visual update; the MotionHandler applies root motion through the chosen collision admission; the late rotation then updates the same ActorState Euler and turn flag. Existing source-reversal-diagnosis.json was a detached kernel/clip probe, so it did not prove this connected Session path.

expected_behavior.preserve: W and S are opposite camera-forward commands. Source phase order applies each sampled local root delta using current facing, then turns toward the newly requested source heading. The same four W/S segments must use one ActorMovement, one CombatSession, one retained source pose owner, and the selected collision path; no speculative lateral clamp or turn smoothing is introduced.
expected_behavior.test_fixture: Use actual KnightPlayerBase Run phase/clip and resolved walk/rotation properties, SemanticInput keyboard mapping, one CombatSession retained locomotion owner, a deterministic camera basis, and a clear synthetic floor CollisionScene. Log per-frame key, move2D, desired heading, facing before/after, local root XYZ, requested world XY, admitted XY, collision move/blocked result and actor/motor position agreement.
expected_behavior.scope_limit: The focused test isolates current input/root/turn integration on clear floor. It is not original native path, dynamic collision, or live campaign verification.

uncertainties: The local v1.0.3 clip uses a virtual stick; it does not encode a reproducible W/S trace or exact reversal intent.
Recovered data is v1.0.2 and version-specific movement differences are unknown.
The user's exact executable/build, camera pose, actor stance, starting facing, input cadence, map location, body scale, and wall/floor contact are unspecified.
The reported behavior is not yet evidence of a source mismatch; source reversals predict lateral arc because root displacement precedes bounded facing updates.

verification_plan.test: C++17 connected same-Session deterministic W,S,W,S replay, 45 frames per held key at 60Hz, using actual Run clip and source-resolved walk/rotation rates. Produce CSV rows with heading, local/world deltas, root motion, collision admission and same-actor transform reconciliation.
verification_plan.branches: Check each key transition releases the prior key; each frame remains on the same Session/actor/pose owner; count admitted and blocked movement; rerun the fixed trace and require byte-identical CSV. The clear-floor fixture expects no blocked samples and does not cover obstacle rejection.
verification_plan.claim_boundary: Report helper/Session proof separately from original-video observation and in-game integration. No main/core/camera changes unless this replay identifies a concrete mismatch against the recovered source order.

verification_result.input_trace: 45 frames W, 45 S, 45 W, 45 S at 60Hz; keyboard adapter produced +1,-1,+1,-1 camera-forward intent

collision.fixture: synthetic clear floor; no wall contacts

verification_result.same_session: ActorState and ActorMovement agreed after each connected CombatSession sample; retained pose owner/lease stayed unchanged

verification_limits: This proves the current connected Session harness reproduces a camera-left arc under the specified alternating keyboard trace; the recovered source order predicts it.
The original video has no visible W/S input trace and does not establish that this particular turn/path should be straight. No source discrepancy was reproduced.
The clear-floor test does not verify live campaign PF/path/obstacle admission or the user's exact executable, camera pose, actor start facing, scale, cadence, or location.
No main/core/camera behavior was edited; this evidence is helper/Session proof, not in-game visual integration acceptance.
implementation_edits: No gameplay implementation changes; added only the evidence report and focused same-Session movement replay test/runner.
